title: Comparison of Two Protocols for the Generation of iPSC-Derived Human Astrocytes
author: Mulica, Venegas, et al.
materials: Human iPSC lines CTRL1 and CTRL2, which were previously generated as described [31, 32], were maintained in mTeSR™ Plus medium. Astrocytes differentiated directly from iPSCs (herein referred to as “LSF method”) were generated as previously described [24, 25]. In short, iPSCs were converted to neuroepithelial cells by maintenance for 11 days in neurodifferentiation medium (NDM) containing 10 µM SB431542 (Sigma) and 200 nM LDN-193189 (Sigma). NDM consisted of DMEM-F12 (Gibco) and Neurobasal (Gibco) in 50:50 ratio supplemented with 1% B27 without vitamin A (Gibco), 0.5% N2 (Gibco), 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco) and 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco). Next, cells were kept for two additional days in NDM supplemented with 25 ng/ml bFGF (Peprotech). Subsequently, cells were dissociated by scraping, plated on ultra-low attachment plates (Corning) and grown for two days in NDM without the addition of growth factors. Under these conditions, cells formed spheres and were maintained in astrodifferentation medium (ADM) for five months, and manually dissociated by cutting once per week. ADM was comprised of DMEM-F12 supplemented with 1% non-essential amino acids (Gibco), 1% N2, 1% GlutaMAX, 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin, 2 µg/ml heparin (Sigma), as well as 10 ng/ml bFGF and 10 ng/ml EGF (Peptrotech). Terminal differentiation was achieved by dissociating the spheres with accutase (Merck Millipore) and plating them on matrigel (Corning)-coated plates, followed by cultivation for 7 days in ADM containing 10 ng/ml CNTF (Peprotech) and 10 ng/ml BMP4 (Peprotech). To obtain biological replicates, spheres were kept separately for at least 1 month and terminal differentiations were started independently.

The alternative two-step protocol referred to as “SSC method” is initiated by the conversion of iPSCs into neural precursor cells (NPCs), by means of dual-SMAD inhibition and induction of WNT and SHH signaling. These cells correspond to neuroepithelial cells that retain the potential to give rise to neural tube and neural crest lineages [32]. After conversion, NPCs were expanded in N2B27 medium consisting of DMEMF-12 (Gibco)/Neurobasal (Gibco) in 50:50 ratio, supplemented with 1% B27 without vitamin A (Gibco), 0.5% N2 (Gibco), 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco) and 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco). Additionally, 3 µM CHIR99201 (Sigma), 0.75 µM purmorphamine (Sigma) and 150 µM ascorbic acid (Sigma) were added to the medium. The second step in this protocol corresponds to the generation of astrocytes from NPCs, as published before [26]. In brief, NPCs were plated and kept in the standard medium for two days. Afterwards, the medium was changed to N2B27 medium containing 3 µM CHIR, 0.75 µM Purmorphamine (PMA), 150 µM ascorbic acid and 20 ng/ml bFGF (Peprotech) for two additional days. At day four, cells were dissociated using accutase and plated in DMEMF-12 supplemented with 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 1% GlutaMAX, 1% N2, 2% B27 with vitamin A (Gibco), 40 ng/ml EGF (Peprotech), 40 ng/ml bFGF and 1.5 ng/ml hLIF (Peprotech). Cells were maintained in this medium for three passages and for terminal differentiation grown in DMEM-F12 containing 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 1% GlutaMAX and 1% FBS (Gibco) for 60–67 days. Biological replicates were prepared by growing and splitting precursor cells separately and subsequently, for each replicate an independent terminal differentiation was conducted.

To perform immunocytochemistry analysis, cells were fixed using 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS (ThermoScientific). Subsequently, cells were permeabilized and blocked with 0.25% Triton X-100 and 1% BSA in PBS for 1 h. The same solution was used to prepare dilutions of primary and secondary antibodies. Primary antibodies were incubated overnight at four degree at the given dilutions: Oct4 (Abcam, ab19857, 1:1000), TRA-1–60 (Merck Millipore, MAB4360, 1:1000), Sox2 (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, sc-365823, 1:1000), Nestin (Novus, MAB1259, 1:1000), Musashi1 (Abcam, ab21628, 1:500), Pax6 (Imtec Diagnostics, 901,301, 1:1000), Sox1 (R&D Systems, AF3369, 1:100), GFAP (Dako, z0334, 1:500), Vimentin (Abcam, ab24525, 1:500). On the following day, after several washing steps, secondary antibodies were applied for three hours and subsequently washed again with PBS. Afterwards, nuclei were stained with 20 µM Hoechst (LifeTechnologies), cells were washed and subjected to imaging. Images of iPSCs and NPCs were acquired with a Zeiss Axio Imager M2, whereas astrocytes were imaged using a Yokogawa CV8000 microscope.

RNA extraction was carried out with the RNeasy Plus Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s instructions. Library preparation and sequencing were performed by the Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) in Copenhagen, Denmark, using the BGISEQ-500 platform.

Raw RNA-seq reads were quality-filtered with the removal of adaptor sequences and contaminating low-quality reads. Furthermore, the base percentage distribution and distribution of quality scores along the reads was checked. Data was subsequently pre-processed, applying the software package "Rsubread" [33]. Gene level differential expression analysis to compare the two astrocytic protocols, LSF and SSC, was conducted in the R statistical programming software using the package "DESeq2" [34]. Genes with low expression counts were excluded with the “filterByExpr-function” using the package edgeR [35] with default parameters. To determine P-value significance scores for differential expression we used the Wald test followed by an adjustment for multiple hypothesis testing with the Benjamini and Hochberg method [36]. Heat maps were generated using the “heatmap.2” function from the R package "gplots" [37].

Firstly, we characterized all iPSC and neural precursor cell (NPC) lines used in the study to ensure their differentiation potential. The iPSC lines did not show any chromosomal aberrations (Figure S1) and thus were employed for the generation of astrocytes. Furthermore, we assessed the expression of several iPSC and NPC markers using immunocytochemistry. Both iPSC lines expressed typical pluripotency markers such as Oct4, TRA-1–60 and Sox2 (Figure S2A). Moreover, the expression of neural progenitor cell markers, such as Musashi1, Nestin, Pax6 and Sox1, was identified in the NPC lines (Figure S2B) rendering them suitable for differentiation.

steps.title: Maintain iPSCs
steps.instruction: Culture human iPSC lines (CTRL1, CTRL2) continuously in mTeSR™ Plus medium under standard conditions.

steps.title: LSF neuroepithelial induction
steps.instruction: Maintain iPSCs for 11 days in neurodifferentiation medium (NDM) composed of DMEM‑F12 and Neurobasal (50:50) supplemented with 1 % B27 without vitamin A, 0.5 % N2, 1 % GlutaMAX, 0.5 % penicillin/streptomycin, 10 µM SB431542 (Sigma) and 200 nM LDN‑193189 (Sigma).

steps.title: LSF early bFGF expansion
steps.instruction: Continue culture for 2 additional days in the same NDM supplemented with 25 ng ml⁻¹ basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF, Peprotech).

steps.title: LSF sphere formation
steps.instruction: Dissociate cells by scraping, plate onto ultra‑low attachment plates (Corning) and grow for 2 days in NDM without any growth factors; cells will aggregate into spheres.

steps.title: LSF long‑term sphere culture
steps.instruction: Maintain spheres in astrodifferentiation medium (ADM) for 5 months, manually cutting/dissociating them once per week.

substeps.instruction: ADM composition: DMEM‑F12 plus 1 % non‑essential amino acids (Gibco), 1 % N2, 1 % GlutaMAX, 0.5 % penicillin/streptomycin, 2 µg ml⁻¹ heparin (Sigma), 10 ng ml⁻¹ bFGF and 10 ng ml⁻¹ EGF (Peprotech).
Keep spheres from each biological replicate in separate dishes for at least 1 month before terminal differentiation.

steps.title: LSF terminal differentiation
steps.instruction: Dissociate spheres with Accutase (Merck Millipore), plate onto Matrigel‑coated plates (Corning) and culture for 7 days in ADM supplemented with 10 ng ml⁻¹ CNTF and 10 ng ml⁻¹ BMP4 (both Peprotech).

substeps.instruction: Perform independent terminal differentiations for each biological replicate.

steps.title: SSC NPC expansion
steps.instruction: Expand iPSC‑derived neural precursor cells (NPCs) in N2B27 medium (DMEM‑F12/Neurobasal 50:50) containing 1 % B27 without vitamin A, 0.5 % N2, 1 % GlutaMAX, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, 3 µM CHIR99201 (Sigma), 0.75 µM purmorphamine (Sigma) and 150 µM ascorbic acid (Sigma).

steps.title: SSC NPC pre‑culture
steps.instruction: Plate NPCs and maintain in the standard N2B27 medium for 2 days.

steps.title: SSC NPC patterning
steps.instruction: Replace medium with N2B27 containing 3 µM CHIR, 0.75 µM purmorphamine, 150 µM ascorbic acid and 20 ng ml⁻¹ bFGF (Peprotech) for an additional 2 days.

steps.title: SSC astrocyte induction
steps.instruction: On day 4, dissociate cells with Accutase and plate in DMEM‑F12 supplemented with 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, 1 % GlutaMAX, 1 % N2, 2 % B27 with vitamin A (Gibco), 40 ng ml⁻¹ EGF (Peprotech), 40 ng ml⁻¹ bFGF and 1.5 ng ml⁻¹ human LIF (Peprotech). Maintain for three passages.

steps.title: SSC terminal differentiation
steps.instruction: Culture the cells for 60–67 days in DMEM‑F12 containing 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, 1 % GlutaMAX and 1 % fetal bovine serum (FBS, Gibco).

substeps.instruction: Prepare biological replicates by growing and splitting precursor cells separately; each replicate undergoes an independent terminal differentiation.

steps.title: Fix cells for ICC
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS (ThermoScientific).

steps.title: Permeabilize and block
steps.instruction: Incubate cells in 0.25 % Triton X‑100 and 1 % BSA in PBS for 1 hour; use the same solution to dilute primary and secondary antibodies.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate overnight at 4 °C with the following primary antibodies at the indicated dilutions: Oct4 (Abcam, ab19857, 1:1000), TRA‑1‑60 (Merck Millipore, MAB4360, 1:1000), Sox2 (Santa Cruz, sc‑365823, 1:1000), Nestin (Novus, MAB1259, 1:1000), Musashi‑1 (Abcam, ab21628, 1:500), Pax6 (Imtec Diagnostics, 901‑301, 1:1000), Sox1 (R&D Systems, AF3369, 1:100), GFAP (Dako, z0334, 1:500), Vimentin (Abcam, ab24525, 1:500).

steps.title: Secondary antibody and nuclear stain
steps.instruction: After several PBS washes, incubate with appropriate secondary antibodies for 3 hours, wash again, then stain nuclei with 20 µM Hoechst (LifeTechnologies) and wash.

steps.title: Image acquisition
steps.instruction: Capture iPSC and NPC images using a Zeiss Axio Imager M2 microscope; acquire astrocyte images with a Yokogawa CV8000 microscope.

steps.title: Astrocyte image analysis
steps.instruction: Run custom Matlab 2020a scripts (IDs 906, 907, 2352‑2354) on the university HPC platform to quantify nuclei and GFAP signals, compute perinuclear GFAP intensity, segment soma and GFAP⁺ protrusions, extract shape descriptors (perimeter, area, ratios) and calculate mean Vimentin intensity within segmented cellular masks.

steps.title: RNA extraction
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA using the RNeasy Plus Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: RNA sequencing
steps.instruction: Submit RNA samples to Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) for library preparation and sequencing on the BGISEQ‑500 platform.

steps.title: RNA‑seq preprocessing
steps.instruction: Quality‑filter raw reads, remove adapter sequences and low‑quality reads, inspect base‑percentage distribution and quality‑score profiles, then process the cleaned data with the Rsubread package.

steps.title: Differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Perform gene‑level differential expression using DESeq2 in R; filter low‑count genes with edgeR’s filterByExpr (default parameters); apply the Wald test and adjust p‑values with the Benjamini‑Hochberg method.

steps.title: Heat‑map generation
steps.instruction: Create heat maps of expression data using the heatmap.2 function from the gplots R package.

steps.title: Pathway enrichment
steps.instruction: Run GeneGo MetaCore™ standard enrichment workflow on the differential expression results; calculate false‑discovery‑rate scores (Benjamini‑Hochberg) for GeneGo pathway maps, process networks and GO gene sets.

steps.title: Bulk RNA deconvolution
steps.instruction: Apply the MuSiC method to estimate cell‑type composition using three reference scRNA‑seq datasets: (i) GSE140231 (snRNA‑seq substantia nigra & cortex), (ii) GSE157783 (snRNA‑seq midbrain PD study), (iii) GSE76381 (embryonic ventral midbrain, 6‑11 weeks); use published cell‑type annotations as references.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental data with GraphPad Prism 9.4.0; use two‑way ANOVA for grouped comparisons and consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
